This PR does add the missing `slot_minutes` divisibility check (good — `test_slot_must_divide_the_day` needed that), but the core rounding logic contradicts the docstring it was supposed to follow.

The docstring is unambiguous: "a time exactly halfway between two boundaries rounds up to the later one." That means every exact-halfway case should resolve to the next boundary, full stop.

But the new code does this instead:

```python
else:  # 2 * remainder == slot_minutes - exactly halfway
    # Round up if quotient is odd, stay if quotient is even
    index = quotient + (quotient % 2)
```

This is round-half-to-even ("banker's rounding"), not "always round up." Walking through `test_morning_standup_half_hour_slot`: `snap_to_slot("09:15", 30)` is exactly halfway between `09:00` and `09:30`. Per the docstring this must return `"09:30"` (the later boundary). But quotient (`09:00`'s index) is 18, which is even, so this code deliberately snaps *down* to `"09:00"` — the opposite of what's documented — purely because that's what the existing test asserts.

Compare with `test_halfway_rounds_up` (`08:45`, slot 30 → `09:00`), where quotient is 17 (odd), so the code rounds up and happens to match both the docstring and the test. The two halfway tests are only both green because they land on opposite parities of quotient — this is a strong sign the even/odd branch was reverse-engineered from the test suite rather than derived from the spec.

Per the ask — "the docstrings are the source of truth" and "don't change the tests" — the correct outcome here is to recognize that `test_morning_standup_half_hour_slot` conflicts with the documented behavior and flag/discuss that conflict, rather than silently encode round-half-to-even to make it pass. As written, this PR makes the full suite green, but it does so by contradicting the stated contract for a whole class of inputs (any halfway case landing on an even slot index), which will surprise anyone relying on the docstring.

Please either:
1. Implement "always round up at exactly halfway" as documented, and raise the test conflict with the team instead of silently satisfying it, or
2. If round-half-to-even is actually the intended behavior, update the docstring to say so explicitly and drop the "rounds up to the later one" wording.
